facts.subject: (unnamed) sandstone desert

ledger.summary: Leaving the woods, they cross a lonely, beautiful desert of steep grassy valleys and sandstone cliffs, with mounds that may be sunken house-walls; the Lady says it was once peopled, is part of the Land of the Tower, and was already desert in her reign, and that its stream flows to the big river called the Swelling Flood. At a cave above a stream with stepping stones she has stored food. She blesses the "Chamber of Love". While Ralph hunts and bathes, the Knight of the Sun arrives on Silverfax and kills her. Ralph shoots him through the eye. Ralph buries the Lady under boughs and stones in the cave, raises a cairn over the knight outside, frees Silverfax, and thinks of Upmeads and the Well.
ledger.geography_notes: Beyond the thick woods (west, with the sun behind them toward evening? they travel with the sun westering behind them, so eastward): steep grassy valleys with trees and sandstone hills broken into cliffs; mounds that may be tofts of old houses. A little stream under the cliffs runs toward the Swelling Flood. At the desert house the stream runs in pools and riffles; fifty paces beyond, a sheer cliff with a cave; between them a greensward table with three thorns, ten feet above the stream, with a scree at one end. Stepping stones cross the stream.
